subject: SEARCH statement
notes: kb/Work PB443 LANDED - BOTH SENTENCES, AT THE RIGHT STAGE, UNDER THE RIGHT NUMBER. Sentence 1 (an OCCURS clause with an INDEXED phrase) was DECIDED before this and then delivered as a BoundUnsupported, which the emitter renders as a run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException - so the program compiled, shipped an assembly and aborted the run unit blaming WiseOwl COBOL for a gap, and on an unexecuted path said nothing at all, where ISO 4.2.2 paragraph 2 puts the indication at compile time; worse, the message miscited itself as SR1 (the reference-modification rule) in BOTH arms. It is now COBOL2075 quoting SR2, with the two halves - no OCCURS at all, and an OCCURS with no INDEXED phrase - given their own sentences. Sentence 2 ("identifier-1 shall not be subscripted at the level for which the SEARCH is applicable") had NO site: the subscripts were discarded with the rest of the written reference, so `SEARCH E(IX)` and `SEARCH E(2)` ran as though `SEARCH E` had been written (measured). It is now an UPPER BOUND on the subscripts AS WRITTEN (ReferenceResolver.SubscriptSegmentsOf, the same declaration-informed splitter SR8/SR9 use): a table-item reference normally takes one subscript per OCCURS level (8.4.2.3), this rule removes the searched level's, so MORE subscripts than identifier-1 has superordinate tables means one sits at that level. NOT a lower bound - see SR-14.9.37.3-3, where reading one into SR3 failed six NIST programs. kb/Work PB444 keeps SR4 (END-SEARCH with NEXT SENTENCE), the one remaining SEARCH syntax rule with no site; kb/Work PB211 keeps SR5 (identifier-2's class).
